label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
**One star for now: our library needs a working system and someone accountable**

Bridger Bend Community Library is a one-branch library with two full-time staff, volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud in June 2026 at $14,200 a year. Our catalog and circulation migration went live October 19.

Since October 28, checkouts have worked only offline on one laptop. Our holds queue was wiped out—approximately 640 holds gone. A support ticket has been open for 12 days. We have received three replies, all saying the issue has been “escalated to engineering.” We still need a resolution.

These failures have consequences beyond an inconvenient workday. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to collect his held large-print Westerns. We had no record of his hold and sent him home with nothing. One of our volunteers has been recording checkouts on index cards. With two full-time staff, we do not have spare capacity to reconstruct records while continuing to serve patrons.

During sales, we were promised “a dedicated migration specialist.” What we received was a shared inbox. That gap between the support promised and the support delivered is central to this review.

To be fair, the software looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is genuinely better than our old system. I can see why libraries would choose it. My concern is not the product idea. It is what happens when something goes badly wrong and a small library needs help.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and our library’s line item is on the agenda. I need to be able to explain what is being done to restore the service we are paying for.

I am asking someone senior at Stackhouse to call me this week, name a person responsible for our case, and provide a recovery plan addressing circulation and the missing holds.

For other library directors: get support response times and escalation commitments in writing before signing. Ask exactly what “dedicated” migration support means.

One star for now. I will revisit this review if Stackhouse resolves these problems.
